Since 1970 the consumer price index for the United States has risen just over 5.5-fold; that is inflation. In Hungary, the index of wholesale prices was 38,500 in January 1923 and 1,026,000 in January 1924, one year later, a 27-fold increase; that is hyperinflation (Sargent 1986, 64).
One of the earliest studies of the dynamics of money and prices during hyperinflation was done by Cagan (1956). The discussion here follows Cagan in using continuous time.
